attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, said in his own voice.

semantics.note: An unqualified 'will' with no deadline. 'Far worse' is a fair rendering of 'by several echelons'. The investor framing comes from the sentence itself.

contract.note: The plain reading (investor harm well beyond the dot-com crash, no multiplier imposed, open horizon, non-occurrence cannot contradict) is ordinary and fair. The loss measure is an evaluator choice.

evidence.note: FactSet, June 2026. Describes how long the dot-com decline lasted; its AI-crash scenarios are hypothetical stress tests, not realized losses.
Sherlund, available 2026-10-25. Shows a two-week AI sell-off of up to 18%. That is not a completed collapse and gives no aggregate loss figure comparable to dot-com.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline. No dated collapse in the packet shows losses well beyond the dot-com crash, and a short sell-off does not meet the early-resolution rule. Without a deadline, non-occurrence cannot contradict it, so it stays open.

attribution.note: Zitron's own present-tense statement in his post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps both parts: Oracle's capacity and OpenAI's money. Both are stated as current fact.

contract.note: Judging at publication against the contract's delivery and payment schedule, rather than demanding full immediate delivery, is a fair reading. The result depends on schedule and liquidity data the speaker did not give.

evidence.note: OpenAI disclosure from July 2025, before the target period. It shows the capacity was still under development and does not prove an inability to deliver.
Reuters, December 12, 2025: a reported delay that Oracle denied. Oracle's denial is a company statement, not independent proof of capacity.
SoftBank disclosure: $22.5B funded on December 26. This is financing received, not proof that OpenAI can meet the Oracle payment schedule.

reviews.rationale: The packet has neither the contract's delivery and payment schedule nor OpenAI's net available funds for December 2025. The delay report was denied, and the new funding does not settle whether OpenAI can pay. Neither part is established or disproved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the hedge 'does not appear'. That wording expresses graded confidence, not a firm assertion that the deal is not happening.

contract.note: The contract applies a plain reading and scores tentative wording. Policy reserves plain-reading scoring for firm language, and the hedge 'does not appear' should not be scored.

evidence.note: Broadcom earnings call, December 2025: Tan calls the 10GW deal an alignment mainly for 2027–2029 and expects little in 2026.
Same call: Tan separates the 10GW alignment from a custom-chip program at an advanced stage that will have a committed element.
October 2025 announcement of a signed term sheet, with deployment from H2 2026 to 2029. Background only.

reviews.rationale: 'Does not appear to be happening' is hedged, graded-confidence language, so it is not scored under policy. Even on its merits the evidence is split: the 10GW deal was a non-binding alignment, but chip development was well advanced.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post.

semantics.note: A firm 'going to' / 'will' forecast with 'eventually' as its only horizon. Both parts are kept.

contract.note: Requiring a failed, withdrawn or unwound package is somewhat strict for 'begin to fall apart', but it is an ordinary reading and the contract flags the ambiguity. Requiring abandonment rather than delay for 'unbuilt' is fair.

evidence.note: Reuters, March 2026: the Oracle/OpenAI Abilene expansion was dropped, but the capacity moved to another campus and other tenants were considered. Not clearly 'unbuilt'.
Crusoe, March 2026: new Abilene development for Microsoft is underway. This weighs against reading the site as abandoned.
Reuters/FT, September 2026: the $18B Project Jupiter loans trade at about 90 cents and their syndication stalled. That is strain, not a confirmed failure or unwinding.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline. The evidence shows a dropped expansion that moved elsewhere and a debt package under strain, but no confirmed abandoned project and no failed or unwound package, so the early-resolution rule is not met. With no deadline, non-occurrence cannot contradict it.
